policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV reads 'And there was set food before him to eat', a passive with no expressed agent, which matches the qere hophal wa-yusam. But the ketiv is written without vowels and its consonants carry no voice distinction: the same letters can be pointed as a passive, so the English passive does not exclude it. No ASV note is mapped to this verse, and nothing else in GEN.24.33 turns on the choice. Both readings remain compatible; the qere base fallback carries the projection.
